The second passage is from George Simpson of the Hudson’s Bay Company, which operated mainly in North America, trading manufactured goods for resources obtained by Indigenous peoples.  
The Hudson’s Bay Company’s primary trade was in furs — especially beaver pelts — which were highly valuable in European markets for making hats and other goods.  
The passage emphasizes making Indigenous traders dependent on European goods, which aligns with the fur trade economy.
